setting: You all live in Glasgow and grew up in Govan, where Gran's flat is. Fiona lives in Giffnock, Callum in Shawlands and Kirsty in Partick, so you see each other often but not every week. Gran died in September and you are clearing the flat together, and you have known each other all your lives. Last week the group chat was about whether Callum's car was parked legally outside the Hampden car park.
opener: Sends a photo of Gran's hall cupboard and asks who can come on Saturday to start the kitchen.

Fiona.knows: You know Callum is the middle one, who always has a plan and rarely finishes it, and Kirsty is the youngest, who you still half think of as the baby.
Fiona.like: You're practical, a bit bossy, and quietly funny in a dry way. You have firm opinions about tea, bins and flat-pack furniture.
Fiona.texts: You message the group now and then, mostly when something needs deciding or sorting.
Fiona.style: You type in full sentences with proper capitals and full stops, and you use a laughing emoji now and then but few abbreviations.

Callum.knows: You know Fiona is the organised one who will have a list, and Kirsty is the youngest, who you still tease but would do anything for.
Callum.like: You're easygoing, sentimental underneath the jokes, and you have strong opinions about football and old wooden furniture.
Callum.texts: You message the group quite often, usually with photos or jokes, and you tend to reply quickly.
Callum.style: You type mostly in lowercase with light punctuation and often send a few short messages in a row.

Kirsty.knows: You know Fiona is the eldest who sorts everyone out and Callum is the middle one who makes you laugh and drives you mad.
Kirsty.like: You're warm, sensible and quick to notice when someone is struggling. You have opinions about council planning rules and good coffee.
Kirsty.texts: You message the group now and then, usually to check on the others or to suggest plans.
Kirsty.style: You type in ordinary sentences with capitals and mostly correct punctuation, use the odd exclamation mark, and rarely abbreviate.

private_lines.Fiona: You are a practice nurse at a health centre in Giffnock and live with your husband Andy and your teenage daughter. You're up around half six, work eight to four, and come home to tea and a bit of telly before bed.
private_lines.Callum: You are a self-employed joiner in Shawlands and live with your partner Lorna in a tenement flat. Your days vary with the jobs, but you're usually up around seven and out by eight, and you're home by six if the work's done.
private_lines.Kirsty: You work in the planning department of the city council and live alone in Partick with a rescue dog. You're up around quarter to seven, work nine to five, and walk the dog along the Kelvin in the evenings.

situation: Siblings clearing out a grandparent's flat.

text:
[photo]

Everything in this cupboard is apparently "for best". Who can come Saturday to start on the kitchen? We need bodies and bin bags.

am in saturday
do we know if the good tin opener is in there
Which good tin opener?
the one she wouldnae let anyone touch
I can come! Not till after lunch though, the dog has a groomer at 10. Is that too late?
After lunch is fine. Callum, what time can you get over?

dunno maybe 11. depends on the job in bearsden
will bring the van
no promises on the tin opener
Kirsty, you're on bin bags. The big ones, not the wee ones she kept under the sink.
Fine. I'll get the 90 litre ones.
found the tin opener in the drawer by the cooker. she had it wrapped in a tea towel
Of course she did.
Bring it Saturday, I'll put it in the box for the charity shop. Not the bin.
its going in my van
Just back from the Kelvin. Dog is soaked and smells like a bin, so that's me sorted for the night.
Wash the dog before you get on the sofa.
Obviously.
was reading the old bills in the hall press. she was still paying for the phone line in 2009 lol
She was never getting rid of that phone line. Andy's still got her number on his list of things to disconnect.
Did anyone find the photos from Dad's sixtieth? I think they might be in the bureau.
Bureau is on the list for Saturday. Don't start on it on your own, we're doing it together.
ye hear that kirsty
Yes Fiona.
Night all. Half six comes early.
Morning. The dog has decided she's coming to Govan on Saturday. I've said no. She's not listening.
bring her. she can sit in the van wi the tin opener
joke. or not. she can come
She is not coming. She'll be under our feet and she'll eat the bin bags.
She'd be a great help with the bags actually
Exactly.

[photo]

is this a chair or a bit of a chair. job in bearsden is a kitchen from 1974. they want it back how it was
they've got an avocado suite n all. i'm no joking
Are the photos in the bureau or not
havent been near the bureau. fi said no
I'm not going near it. Just asking.
Off shift. Bureau is Saturday. Both of you.
home. lorna says is the carpet still in the front room
i said dunno
Carpet's coming up when the man comes. Whenever that is.
Walked the dog round the Kelvin again. Ducks everywhere. Gran's chair is still in the front window and it got me this morning when I was on the phone to the bank. Felt daft.
aye. i sat in it wi the telly on the other night and then felt daft
Front room last. Give it a day.
Thanks.
how's the tin opener box
In my hall. Callum, you can take it home tonight if you're going to fuss about it.
its going in the van sat
Bed.
fi you still up
Asleep, Callum, like a normal person. What's wrong?
Morning. Is everyone alright? Callum you sounded tired on the Kelvin last night, or I'm imagining it.
nothing. couldnae sleep. just sat wi the chair for a bit
no the lights on i know
Next time sit in the chair with the telly off and go to bed after. That's my advice.
noted
That's good advice actually.
Sitting in a meeting about a conservatory on a listed tenement in Hyndland. The man has brought a sketch in a Greggs bag.
did he get the bag from the greggs in the bag?
I refuse to answer that.
bearsden people have decided to keep the avocado. the wife says its "a feature now". i said its a fire hazard. she said sit down
Off shift. Had a man in asking for a sick note for his dog. Sent him to the vet. Kirsty, if your dog wants a note, she can get one from me.
She does not need a note. She's had a great week.
Good for her.
home. lorna's asked again about the carpet. tell her fi
Carpet's coming up Saturday when the man comes, if the man comes. Tell Lorna I said so.
ye hear that lorna
Just in. Has anyone got a plan for the bureau or are we just going to stand in front of it on Saturday looking at it?
We're going to open it, one drawer at a time, with the three of us there. Like adults.
i'll bring a crowbar just in case
You'll bring nothing. The bureau's not getting a crowbar.
If the photos are in there I want to be the one who finds them.
fine by me. i'll be the one who finds the tin opener's receipt
Callum, you'll be the one who makes the tea.
Bed soon. Tin opener is in the hall box with a label on it in my writing. Nobody touch it.
Night all. Dog has already gone to sleep on my good cushion. Not going to fight it.
fi you still up
